decisions.selected: Measure remediation of cache-strategy findings rather than workflow activity.
decisions.rationale: The adoption-time mission is to identify repeated cache problems and raise actionable issues; creation alone is not repository attainment.

decisions.selected: Assign the linked [cache-strategy] issues whose bodies name the workflow run URL.
alternatives: Assign every cache-memory workflow examined that day
decisions.rationale: The issue template embeds the producing run URL, which provides a stable, reconstructable ownership key without relying on agent logs.

decisions.selected: Accept a linked issue closed as completed.
decisions.rationale: Completed issue state is durable repository evidence of the assigned remediation; logs and output creation are activity evidence.

decisions.selected: Use completed linked issues divided by linked issues.
decisions.rationale: The proportion measures full attainment for all findings assigned to one run without combining operational attainment with diagnostics.
The workflow allows seven days for safe issue output, so a fixed thirty-day horizon preserves a post-output remediation window and stable observations.
The workflow was introduced in its adoption commit and no pre-adoption workflow cases exist to score under this contract.

uncertainties.description: GitHub issue search or issue-state evidence can be unavailable during replay.
uncertainties.mitigation: Return null rather than treating unavailable evidence as a missed remediation.

uncertainties.description: A completed issue does not establish that this workflow caused the remediation.
